publication_endpoint: independent test of capture-time migratory readiness x landscape resistance on later movement expression
core_hypothesis: realised migration has separable initiation and completion stages: internal readiness governs initiation; route-specific ecological context is hypothesized to govern post-initiation fate

primary_cohort.rationale: each stage has >=98 individuals across 7 projects with complete WRS-table coverage

boundary_groups.FII: n=17; 16/17 from one project, descriptive boundary only
boundary_groups.silver: coarse stage label; not pooled into ordinal Durif analysis

primary_predictions: capture-time Durif stage strongly predicts whether classified downstream migration begins
after initiation, the general Durif-stage advantage weakens substantially
barrier/hydrological opportunity should explain variation in post-initiation completion in an independent within-landscape system

primary_estimands.stage_effect: effect of capture-time Durif stage on later movement expression

falsification: independent data fail to reproduce the readiness effect on initiation
post-initiation completion remains equally stage-dominated after barrier/opportunity control
route-specific opportunity does not explain post-initiation heterogeneity
evidence_boundary: aggregate successful-migrant counts by stage were inspected during development; Europe-wide panel is independent developmental evidence, not outcome-blind confirmation
eog_role: discovery of an extreme resident anchor only
